question: The College of Fort William was established at ______ under British rule.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The College of Fort William was established in **Calcutta** in 1800 by the British East India Company.
 
• This institution was founded by **Lord Wellesley**, the then Governor-General of India.
 
• The college aimed to train British civil servants in Indian languages and laws.
 
• It played a significant role in the **promotion of Oriental studies** and the translation of classical Indian texts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Wellesley**:

 
 
• Governor-General of India from 1798 to 1805.
 
• He implemented significant administrative reforms and expanded British territories in India.
 
 
 
• **Oriental Studies**:
 
 
• An academic field focusing on the languages, cultures, history, and societies of Asia.
 
• It includes the study of classical languages such as Sanskrit, Persian, and Arabic.
 
 
 
• **Translation of Classical Texts**:
 
 
• Key classical texts were translated into English, including the Mahabharata and the Ramayana.
 
• This helped in making Indian literature accessible to the Western world.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Education**:
 
 
• The College of Fort William set a precedent for higher education institutions in India.
 
• It laid the foundation for modern educational practices and the study of Indian languages and culture.
